title: Credit Reporting Standard: Tri-Merge Report Reuse and the Credit Report Fee on a Mortgage Loan File
content:
**1. One report per borrower, reused.** Larkspur pulls one tri-merge credit report per borrower and reuses it across every Mortgage Loan File of the same customer while it is valid.

**2. When a fee may be charged.** A credit report fee is charged on a new loan file only after the credit report validity window that started on the customer's latest credit report fee charge has run out. The window is counted in calendar days from the entry date of the customer's latest credit report fee charge on any Larkspur loan file; that entry date is day zero and the report stays reusable through the last day of the window. The length of the window is the program's credit report age limit in calendar days (the maximum age of a credit report for use on a note, set in the underwriting schedule). The evidence is the system's fee records of the customer — the entry dates of every credit report fee charge across all of the customer's files — not the customer's recollection of when credit was last pulled.

**3. Inside the window.** Inside the window the existing report is reissued to the new file at no charge and no fee record is booked.

**4. Outside the window.** The clause "Outside the window (or when the customer has no earlier charge) a new pull is made and the fee booked is credit report fee per borrower of the file's program times the number of borrowers pulled" is no longer in force for a credit report pulled again on an existing loan file at the borrower's authorization, and only for such a repull; the charge for such a repull is no longer worked out under it. Every other pull made outside the window or for a customer with no earlier charge, including the first pull on a new loan file, is still charged the credit report fee per borrower of the file's program times the number of borrowers pulled.

**5. Nature of the fee.** The credit report fee is a bona fide third-party charge and may be collected before the Loan Estimate is delivered; it is never refunded once the report has been pulled.

## Counting the window (hypothetical dates, 120-day window)

| Customer's latest credit report fee charge | Day of the new file's credit need | Day number | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| booked on 1 March | 29 June | day 120 | still inside the window: report reissued, no fee record |
| booked on 1 March | 30 June | day 121 | window has run out: a credit report fee may be charged |

Under a 90-day window (the Larkspur Jumbo 30-Year Fixed program's credit report age limit) the last reusable day is day 90 and day 91 is the first day outside the window.

## Points of judgement

- **What is charged for the first pull on a new loan file when the customer has no earlier charge?** The credit report fee per borrower of the file's program times the number of borrowers pulled; under a program whose fee is 92.40 USD, a hypothetical new file with two borrowers pulled is charged 184.80 USD.

- **Which files are searched for the latest charge?** Every Larkspur loan file of the customer, not only the new file.
- **Is a report reissued inside the window billed at a reduced rate?** No. It is reissued at no charge, and no fee record is booked.
- **Can a credit report fee be refunded when the borrower withdraws?** No. Once the report has been pulled the fee is never refunded.
